newsitem.title: USA: CTC sees slower 1998 EPS growth.
newsitem.headline: CTC sees slower 1998 EPS growth.

text.p: CTC Communications Corp said Tuesday that its transition into a full-scale reseller of local telephone services was happening faster than anticipated and could likely dampen fiscal 1998 earnings growth to a range between 20 percent and 25 percent.
CTC said the transition would occur in the first calendar quarter of 1998 rather than the summer of that year.
"This opportunity is coming faster and sooner than planned," it said in a statement. "The company will be incurring unanticipated expenses in regard to advancing its transition date."

CTC, which had originally expected 30 percent to 40 percent growth in earnings, said the acceleration was prompted by competition and state regulatory decisions on wholesale tariffs, among other factors.
Eighteen months after the start of the resale transition, the company's annual revenue run rate is expected to be $200 million, and $400 million after 30 months, it said.
CTC had about $43 million in annual revenues before the transition.
